chilla-jeep-safari.title: Chilla Range – Rajaji National Park | Chilla Jeep Safari/Jungle Safari

blocks.text: About Chilla Range

**Chilla Range** is one of the most popular safari areas of **Rajaji National Park (Rajaji Tiger Reserve)**, located on the **Haridwar–Rishikesh bypass road**, approximately **10 km from Haridwar and 20 km from Rishikesh**, **Uttarakhand**. Its diverse landscape of dense **Sal forests, open grasslands and riverine habitats** provides visitors with an opportunity to experience the natural beauty and wildlife of Rajaji.

The **Chilla Jeep Safari** follows an approximately **2 hours 30 minutes route**, covering scenic forest areas around **Mundal**, **Mithawali and Khara**. Depending on the season and natural conditions, visitors may encounter **Asian Elephants, deer, Wild Boar, birds and other wildlife**. Wildlife sightings are not guaranteed and depend on animal movement, weather, season and other natural factors.

Short halts at **Mundal and Ghasiram machans (watchtowers)** provide opportunities to observe the surrounding forest landscape and wildlife. The **Chilla Complex** also includes an **Interpretation Centre and Library**, offering visitors an opportunity to learn more about the area's wildlife, forests and conservation.
Chilla Safari Landscape and Wildlife

A **Chilla Jungle Safari** offers a varied experience across forest, grassland and riverine habitats. The approximately **36 km circular safari route**, where applicable, passes through different landscapes associated with the Chilla area and the Ganga. This habitat diversity supports a variety of wildlife and makes the zone particularly attractive for wildlife enthusiasts, photographers and birdwatchers.

Chilla has an important place in the conservation history of the region. It was originally notified as a **wildlife sanctuary in 1977** and was later incorporated with the Rajaji and Motichur sanctuaries to form **Rajaji National Park in 1983**. Rajaji was subsequently designated as a **Tiger Reserve in 2015**.

Chilla serves as an important gateway to the Rajaji landscape and is conveniently accessible from both **Haridwar and Rishikesh, making it a popular choice for visitors** looking to experience a **Rajaji National Park Jeep Safari (Jungle safari in Rajaji Tiger Reserve)**.
Wildlife You Can See on a Chilla Safari

The diverse habitats of **Chilla Range**, including Sal forests, open grasslands, riverine areas and the Ganga landscape, support a wide variety of wildlife. During a **Chilla Jeep Safari in Rajaji National Park**, visitors may have opportunities to observe mammals, birds and reptiles in their natural surroundings.

rows: Asian Elephant, Wild Boar, Sloth Bear
Great Hornbill, Kingfishers, Eagles, Peafowl, Quails, Falcons, Vultures and many other forest and riverine birds

blocks.text: Wildlife Tracking During Chilla Safari

Early morning safaris can offer good opportunities to observe wildlife activity, particularly when animals are moving through forest tracks and open areas. Experienced **nature guides** can also help visitors identify signs of wildlife such as **pugmarks, tracks, feeding signs and elephant activity**.

Rather than focusing only on a particular animal sighting, a **Chilla Jungle Safari** offers the opportunity to observe the wider forest ecosystem and understand the behaviour, habitats and signs of wildlife found in **Rajaji Tiger Reserve**.

Chilla is known for offering an **elephant safari experience in addition to the jeep safari**, subject to the availability and operating arrangements of the Forest Department. An elephant safari provides a different way to experience the forest, with a slower-paced journey through the Chilla landscape.

The elephant safari is generally associated with an **early-morning experience** and may cover a shorter route than the jeep safari. Visitors can enjoy the forest environment, vegetation and wildlife signs from a different perspective. As with any wildlife experience, animal sightings are not guaranteed and visitors should follow the instructions of the mahout, guide and forest authorities.
A combination of **jeep and elephant safari**, where available, offers two distinct ways to explore the Chilla landscape.

Safari Rules & Photography Tips
Enjoy your **Jeep Safari** responsibly and follow all Forest Department rules and instructions from your guide or mahout.

items: **Stay inside the Gypsy or remain on the elephant** throughout the safari. Do not step out of the vehicle or leave the designated safari route.
**Maintain silence near wildlife** and avoid sudden movements, shouting or loud noises. Quiet observation helps minimise disturbance to animals.
**Follow photography rules and permit requirements.** Avoid using flash near wildlife, as sudden flashes may disturb or startle animals.
**Wear comfortable, neutral-coloured clothing** such as khaki, olive, beige or brown, and carry binoculars, sunscreen and a hat for added comfort.
**Carry a light jacket during winter morning safaris**, as temperatures can be cool, particularly during the early hours.
**Do not feed, chase or attempt to attract wildlife** for photographs. Maintain a safe and respectful distance from animals.
**Follow your guide's instructions at all times**, particularly when wildlife is nearby or when stopping at designated viewing points.
**Avoid littering** and carry back all permitted waste to help keep the forest clean.

blocks.text: Rajaji National Park Jeep Safari from Ranipur Gate

The **Haridwar Zone, accessed through Ranipur Gate**, is one of the safari entry points for exploring **Rajaji National Park** (**Rajaji Tiger Reserve**) near Haridwar, Uttarakhand. Located close to the Ranipur and BHEL area, the zone offers visitors an opportunity to explore the Shivalik forest landscape by Jeep Safari.

The Ranipur landscape combines mixed forest, open grassland patches, small hills and seasonal streams, creating varied habitats for wildlife and birds. During a safari, visitors may encounter Asian Elephants, Spotted Deer, Sambar Deer, Nilgai, Barking Deer, Wild Boar and a variety of forest birds.

Leopards also occur in the wider forest landscape around Ranipur, making the area relevant for visitors searching for a **leopard safari near Haridwar**. However, wildlife sightings are never guaranteed and depend on animal movement, season, weather, habitat conditions and other natural factors.

**Safari Duration:** Approximately 2 hours
**Safari Route:** Approximately 25 km
**Safari Type:** Guided Jeep / Gypsy Safari
**Location:** Ranipur Gate, Haridwar, Uttarakhand
Ranipur Gate Jeep Safari Experience

A **Ranipur Gate Jeep Safari** takes visitors through a relatively varied forest setting, with stretches of woodland, grassland patches and hilly terrain. The route provides opportunities to experience the natural character of the **Rajaji Tiger Reserve** while travelling through designated safari tracks.

The landscape is particularly interesting for visitors who enjoy **wildlife photography, birdwatching and nature observation**. Depending on conditions, visitors may see deer, elephants, wild boar and a variety of woodland birds, while the quieter parts of the forest provide suitable habitat for larger carnivores.

Rather than focusing only on wildlife sightings, the Ranipur safari also offers an opportunity to observe the **forest ecosystem, vegetation, hills, seasonal watercourses and changing landscapes** of Rajaji.
**Please remember:** Every safari is different, and seeing a tiger, leopard, elephant or any other particular species cannot be guaranteed.
Leopard Safari near Haridwar

Ranipur is an option for visitors specifically looking for a **leopard safari near Haridwar**. Leopards are naturally present within the forest landscape, but they are elusive animals and sightings can be unpredictable.

A safari should therefore be approached as a **wildlife and nature experience**, rather than as a guaranteed leopard-viewing trip. Animal movement, vegetation, weather, time of day and other ecological conditions all influence what visitors may encounter.
Following the instructions of the authorised safari driver, nature guide and forest authorities helps ensure a safe and responsible wildlife experience.

blocks.text: Explore the forests of Chillawali Range through Mohand Gate and experience a peaceful Rajaji wildlife safari in the Shivalik foothills.
About Mohand Gate – Chillawali Zone

**Chillawali Zone**, accessed through **Mohand Gate**, is a forest tourism area of **Rajaji National Park (Rajaji Tiger Reserve), Uttarakhand**. Located near Ganeshpur on the **Dehradun–Haridwar highway**, the zone offers visitors an opportunity to explore the scenic **Shivalik foothill forests of the Chillawali Range** by Jeep Safari.

Compared with some of the busier safari areas, the **Mohand–Chillawali landscape** offers a relatively peaceful forest experience, with quiet trails, wooded surroundings and varied habitats. The area is particularly interesting for **wildlife enthusiasts, birdwatchers, photographers and nature lovers**, with opportunities to look for leopards and other wildlife along the safari route.
Leopard and other wildlife sightings, however, are **not guaranteed**. Sightings depend on animal movement, season, weather, habitat conditions and other natural factors.
Chillawali Jeep Safari – Leopard Safari

A **Chillawali Jeep Safari through Mohand Gate** offers visitors an opportunity to explore the forest habitats of **Rajaji National Park (Rajaji Tiger Reserve)** and observe wildlife in its natural surroundings.

The safari route passes through the Chillawali and Andheri Rau forest areas, with routes towards the Dholkhand Forest Rest House. The landscape features Sal, Shisham and Rohini forests, open clearings, seasonal streams and the gently undulating terrain of the Shivalik foothills, providing habitat for a variety of birds and wildlife.

Located on the **Dehradun side of Rajaji**, the **Mohand–Chillawali** landscape provides a quieter forest setting away from the Ganga-side landscapes of the reserve. The area is suitable for **wildlife watching, birding, nature photography and family safaris**, with opportunities to look for leopards and other forest wildlife.

During the safari, visitors should follow the instructions of the authorised nature guide, safari driver and forest authorities. Maintaining a safe distance from wildlife, avoiding unnecessary noise and respecting the natural environment are essential for a responsible safari experience.
**Leopard and other wildlife sightings are not guaranteed** and depend on animal movement, season, weather, habitat conditions and other natural factors.

blocks.text: About Motichur Safari Zone

**Motichur Safari Zone** is a popular safari area of **Rajaji National Park, Uttarakhand**, located along the **Haridwar–Rishikesh route**. The zone offers a **Motichur Jeep Safari** through **Sal forests, grasslands and other natural habitats**, providing opportunities to experience the landscape and wildlife of Rajaji.

Motichur was one of the former wildlife sanctuaries that, together with **Rajaji and Chilla**, became part of **Rajaji National Park in 1983**. The area is characterised by **Sal (Shorea robusta) forests, open clearings and varied forest habitats**.

The approximately **25 km safari route** offers opportunities to observe **Asian Elephant, Spotted Deer (Chital), Sambar, Barking Deer, Wild Boar, Hanuman Langur and a variety of forest birds**. Leopards also occur in the wider forest landscape, but **sightings are not guaranteed** and depend on animal movement, season, weather and other natural factors.

A Motichur Jungle Safari is ideal for wildlife enthusiasts, birdwatchers, photographers and families, offering opportunities to explore dense Sal forests and open habitats while observing wildlife and birds in their natural surroundings. An authorised nature guide can enrich the experience by helping visitors understand the forest ecosystem and identify wildlife, birds and signs along the safari route. Visitors should maintain a safe and respectful distance from wildlife and follow the instructions of the safari driver, authorised nature guide and Forest Department at all times.

jhilmil-jheel-safari.title: Jhilmil Jheel Safari – Rajaji National Park
kicker: Jhilmil Jheel Safari Zone & Conservation Reserve

blocks.text: Jhilmil Jheel Conservation Reserve

Jhilmil Jheel Conservation Reserve is a scenic wetland and wildlife destination in Haridwar District, Uttarakhand, situated on the left bank of the River Ganga in the Chiriyapur forest landscape. The area was declared a Conservation Reserve in 2005 and covers approximately 37.84 sq. km.

The reserve features a diverse mosaic of wetlands, grasslands, riverine habitats, tropical mixed moist deciduous forests and scrubland. Its wetland landscape includes old river channels, seasonal and perennial marshes and an oxbow-lake system associated with the Ganga.

Jhilmil Jheel is particularly important for the Swamp Deer (Barasingha) and is recognised as an important habitat for the species in Uttarakhand. The reserve also supports Asian Elephants, Spotted Deer, Sambar, Wild Boar, Nilgai, Leopard and other wildlife, although sightings vary according to season and natural conditions.

The reserve is also an attractive destination for birdwatching and nature observation. A preliminary checklist published by the Uttarakhand Forest Department recorded 238 bird species from Jhilmil Jheel Conservation Reserve.
Wildlife sightings are natural encounters and cannot be guaranteed.
Jhilmil Jheel Safari
A Jhilmil Jheel Safari offers visitors an opportunity to explore the reserve's varied landscapes, including grasslands, wetlands, riverine areas, forest patches and scrub habitats.

The safari is particularly interesting for visitors hoping to observe Swamp Deer, elephants, deer, birds and wetland landscapes. Designated observation areas and watchtowers may provide opportunities for wildlife and bird observation, subject to Forest Department regulations, accessibility and local conditions.
Jhilmil Jheel is suitable for families, birdwatchers, wildlife enthusiasts, photographers and nature lovers.
Why Visit Jhilmil Jheel?

items: 🐘 Opportunities to observe Asian Elephants and other wildlife
🌿 Diverse wetland, grassland, riverine and forest habitats
🔭 Opportunities for wildlife observation from designated viewpoints
📍 A distinctive wildlife destination in Haridwar District, Uttarakhand
📸 Excellent opportunities for nature and bird photography

blocks.text: Birdwatching at Jhilmil Jheel
Jhilmil Jheel is an interesting birdwatching destination because of the combination of wetlands, grasslands, riverine habitats, forest patches and scrubland.

The Uttarakhand Forest Department's preliminary checklist documented 238 bird species from the Conservation Reserve. The recorded diversity includes wetland birds, waders, raptors, forest birds and other resident and migratory species.
Depending on the season, water conditions and bird activity, visitors may encounter kingfishers, waterbirds, waders, raptors, woodpeckers, flycatchers, larks and many other species.
For birdwatchers, early morning is generally a productive period for observation because bird activity is often higher during the cooler hours.

blocks.label: Tip
blocks.text: Carry binoculars and a camera with an appropriate telephoto lens, while maintaining a safe distance from wildlife.
Jhilmil Jheel Safari Route
A Jhilmil Jheel safari provides an opportunity to travel through a landscape of grasslands, wetland surroundings, riverine habitats, forest patches and scrubland.
The open grasslands and wetland areas are particularly important components of the reserve's wildlife habitat and are associated with species such as Swamp Deer, Spotted Deer and Sambar.
The safari route and areas accessible to visitors may change according to Forest Department regulations, seasonal conditions, wildlife movement, weather and management requirements.
Visitors should always follow the instructions issued by the Forest Department and safari staff.
Jhilmil Jheel Safari Vehicle & Guide
Visitors should use the designated safari arrangements permitted by the Forest Department. Current access, vehicle and entry arrangements may vary according to Forest Department regulations.
A trained nature guide can enhance the safari experience by helping visitors identify birds, wildlife, vegetation and important habitats and by explaining local conservation practices.

About Rajaji Tiger Reserve

Rajaji National Park, located in Uttarakhand, India, is a significant wildlife conservation landscape representing the rich biodiversity of the Shiwalik hills and Himalayan foothills. The park was established in 1983 by merging three wildlife sanctuaries — Rajaji, Motichur and Chilla. It was named in honour of Late Shri C. Rajagopalachari, popularly known as “Rajaji,” a distinguished freedom fighter and the first Governor-General of independent India.

The national park covers 820.42 sq. km. In 2015, an additional 255.63 sq. km of adjoining reserved forest was incorporated as a buffer zone, bringing the total area to approximately 1,075 sq. km and resulting in the designation of Rajaji Tiger Reserve under the provisions of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.

Situated along the Shiwalik ranges and their foothills, the reserve encompasses a diverse landscape of forested hills, rugged ridges, deep ravines, river valleys and grasslands. It extends across the Dehradun and Pauri Garhwal districts of Uttarakhand and the adjoining Saharanpur region. Its proximity to Dehradun, Haridwar and the yoga city Rishikesh further enhances its ecological importance, supporting regional biodiversity, watershed protection and environmental balance.

The park's geography is shaped by the Ganges River, the Chilla River and numerous seasonal streams descending from the Shiwalik ridges. The Rajaji and Motichur forest areas are contiguous, while the Chilla area lies to the southeast, separated by the Ganges and Chilla rivers. Many seasonal streams remain dry for much of the year but transform into fast-flowing torrents during the monsoon, creating distinctive riverine habitats.

Rajaji National Park supports a mosaic of forest types, ranging from semi-evergreen and deciduous forests to mixed broad-leaved woodland and Terai grasslands. Its vegetation falls within the Indus-Ganges Monsoon Forest type, with majestic Sal (Shorea robusta) forests dominating large areas. This varied landscape provides important habitats for diverse wildlife and reinforces the reserve's role in biodiversity conservation across the Shiwalik landscape.
Rajaji National Park is open to visitors only from 15th November to 15th June (Chilla, Ranipur, Mohand ranges).
Overview

Rajaji Tiger Reserve, renowned for its scenic landscapes and rich biodiversity, is a major attraction for nature lovers and wildlife enthusiasts. The reserve is located along the hills and foothills of the Shiwalik ranges and represents the characteristic Shiwalik ecosystem. The vegetation of the area comprises a wide range of forest types, including semi-evergreen, moist and dry deciduous, mixed broad-leaved forests, and Terai grasslands. Floristically, the region falls under the Indus–Ganges Monsoon Forest type.

The reserve is predominantly characterized by extensive stands of Sal (Shorea robusta), which form the major forest component across large parts of the landscape. Its position within the transition zone between the temperate Western Himalaya and the Central Himalaya contributes significantly to the high species diversity and enhances the overall wildlife sighting potential.

Rajaji Tiger Reserve supports a sizeable population of Tigers and Asian Elephants and is home to a diverse assemblage of wildlife. The reserve harbours species such as Leopard, Jungle Cat, Himalayan Black Bear, Sloth Bear, Striped Hyena, Goral, Sambar, Wild Pig, Spotted Deer, Barking Deer, among many others. It also provides important habitat for a variety of bird groups, including Vultures, Woodpeckers, Hornbills, and numerous migratory species.

The aquatic ecosystems formed by rivers and streams flowing through the reserve support the breeding of approximately 42 species of fishes. In addition, the reserve sustains a rich diversity of reptiles, including King Cobra, Vipers, Common Krait, Burmese Python, and several other herpetofaunal species.

wildlife.title: Wildlife & Biodiversity of Rajaji Tiger Reserve

blocks.text: Explore the Rich Wildlife and Biodiversity of Rajaji

Rajaji Tiger Reserve in Uttarakhand is a diverse wildlife landscape extending across the Shivalik hills and adjoining riverine and foothill habitats. Its forests, grasslands, river valleys, scrublands and wooded areas support a wide variety of mammals, birds, reptiles, butterflies and plant species.

The landscape is particularly known for its Asian Elephants, Bengal Tigers, leopards, deer, wild boar, langurs and rich birdlife. The varied vegetation and habitats also provide suitable conditions for reptiles, butterflies and numerous native plant species.

During a Rajaji Jeep Safari, visitors can explore different habitats and observe wildlife in their natural surroundings. Wildlife sightings depend on animal movement, season, weather and other natural conditions and are not guaranteed.
Wildlife & Biodiversity of Rajaji Tiger Reserve

The biodiversity of Rajaji is closely associated with the variety of habitats found across the reserve. Sal forests, mixed deciduous forests, riverine vegetation, grasslands, scrublands and forest edges provide food, shelter and habitat for many species.
The reserve landscape is also important for the conservation of Asian Elephants and Bengal Tigers, along with numerous other mammals, birds, reptiles, butterflies and plant species.
Explore the major groups of wildlife and biodiversity found in Rajaji:
🐘 Mammals of Rajaji

Rajaji supports a diverse range of mammals, including Asian Elephant, Bengal Tiger, Leopard, Chital, Sambar, Barking Deer, Wild Boar, Goral, Nilgai and Hanuman Langur, along with other forest-dwelling mammals.
🐦 Birds of Rajaji

The varied habitats of Rajaji provide suitable conditions for a rich diversity of birds. Visitors may encounter hornbills, woodpeckers, kingfishers, parakeets, bulbuls, raptors, waterbirds and many other forest and riverine birds.
Rajaji is also a rewarding destination for birdwatching, particularly along forest edges, grasslands, rivers and open areas.
🐍 Reptiles of Rajaji
Rajaji's forests, streams, rocky areas, grasslands and riverine habitats support a variety of reptiles, including snakes, lizards and other reptiles.
Species such as the Indian Cobra, King Cobra, Indian Rock Python, Common Krait and Indian Monitor Lizard are among the reptiles associated with the Rajaji landscape.
🦋 Butterflies of Rajaji
The flowering plants, forest clearings, grasslands, forest edges and riverine habitats of Rajaji provide suitable conditions for a variety of butterflies.

Commonly recorded or reported species include Blue Pansy, Blue Tiger, Common Crow, Common Mormon, Common Palmfly, Great Eggfly, Lemon Pansy, Peacock Pansy, Plain Tiger, Orange Oakleaf and Tailed Jay, among others.
Butterflies contribute to pollination and form an important part of the food web and ecological diversity of the reserve.
🌿 Flora of Rajaji
The vegetation of Rajaji includes Sal forests, mixed deciduous forests, riverine vegetation, grasslands, scrublands and other forest communities.
This diverse plant cover provides food, shelter and habitat for wildlife while supporting important ecological processes across the reserve.
Diverse Habitats of Rajaji
One of the important features of Rajaji Tiger Reserve is the variety of habitats found within its landscape. These include:
This habitat diversity contributes to the rich wildlife and plant diversity of the reserve.
Wildlife Experience in Rajaji

A Rajaji Jeep Safari offers an opportunity to explore the forest landscape and observe wildlife in natural surroundings. Depending on the season, habitat and location, visitors may encounter elephants, deer, wild boar, langurs, birds, reptiles and butterflies.
Predators such as tigers and leopards occur in the Rajaji landscape, but sightings are naturally unpredictable and cannot be guaranteed.
Visitors should follow the instructions of nature guides and safari drivers and maintain a respectful distance from wildlife.

birds.title: Birds of Rajaji National Park and Bird Watching

blocks.text: Wildlife in Rajaji – Book Your Jungle Safari / Jeep Safari

Rajaji National Park, also known as Rajaji Tiger Reserve, is a fascinating destination for birdwatching in Uttarakhand, supporting approximately 400 species of birds across its diverse forest, grassland and riverine habitats.

The reserve's varied habitats, including Sal forests, mixed deciduous forests, grasslands, riverine areas, forest edges and open clearings, support a diverse assemblage of resident, migratory and altitudinal migrant birds. The location of Rajaji along the Shivalik foothills and at the transition between Himalayan and Gangetic landscapes further contributes to its varied birdlife.

During a Rajaji Jeep Safari / Jungle Safari, visitors may observe colourful forest birds, birds of prey, woodpeckers, hornbills, kingfishers, parakeets, pheasants and other birds in their natural surroundings. The combination of forest, grassland and riverine habitats makes Rajaji an appealing destination for birdwatchers, nature enthusiasts and wildlife photographers.
Bird Watching in Rajaji National Park and Uttarakhand

Explore the fascinating birdlife of **Rajaji National Park and the surrounding Uttarakhand landscape** through birdwatching and wildlife safari experiences. Depending on the **season, habitat and weather conditions**, visitors may encounter a variety of **resident, migratory and altitudinal migrant birds**.

The Indian Peafowl, India's national bird, is commonly observed in suitable habitats of the reserve. Other birds recorded or associated with the Rajaji landscape include the Rusty-cheeked Scimitar Babbler, Golden-spectacled Warbler, Chestnut-tailed Starling, Brown Hawk-Owl, Brown Fish Owl, Drongo Cuckoo, Slaty-headed Parakeet, Great Hornbill, Red Junglefowl, Lineated Barbet, Black-hooded Oriole and Kalij Pheasant, along with numerous woodpeckers, kingfishers, barbets, finches, thrushes and other forest birds.
Winter can provide additional birdwatching opportunities as migratory and altitudinal migrant species occur in suitable habitats, wetlands and water bodies around the Rajaji landscape.

Birdwatching in Rajaji offers visitors an opportunity to experience the reserve beyond its famous large mammals and appreciate the diversity of forest, grassland and riverine ecosystems that support its rich birdlife.

blocks.text: Rajaji Tiger Reserve in Uttarakhand supports a rich diversity of butterflies. Its varied habitats, including Sal forests, grasslands, riverine areas, forest edges, open clearings and flowering plant communities, provide suitable conditions for a wide range of butterfly species.
During a Rajaji Jeep Safari, visitors may observe colourful butterflies along forest trails, grasslands, sunny clearings, forest edges and areas with flowering vegetation.
Butterfly Species of Rajaji National Park
Commonly recorded or reported butterfly species associated with the Rajaji landscape include:

Blue Pansy, Blue Tiger, Common Bush Brown, Common Castor, Common Crow, Common Emigrant, Common Evening Brown, Common Five-ring, Common Grass Yellow, Common Jay, Common Mormon, Common Palmfly, Common Pierrot, Common Pioneer, Common Sailer, Danaid Eggfly, Great Eggfly, Lemon Pansy, Lime Swallowtail, Orange Oakleaf, Pea Blue, Peacock Pansy, Plain Tiger, Psyche, Indian Wanderer and Tailed Jay.
This is an indicative list rather than a complete checklist. Butterfly occurrence can vary between locations, seasons and habitats within Rajaji Tiger Reserve.

Butterflies play important ecological roles as pollinators and as part of the food web. Their diversity is also associated with the variety of vegetation and habitats found across the Rajaji landscape.
Best Time for Butterfly Watching in Rajaji
Butterflies are generally more active during warm, sunny conditions, particularly around forest edges, grasslands, flowering plants, riverine habitats and sunny clearings.
Morning hours can be particularly suitable for butterfly watching and photography, when many species become active as temperatures rise.
Butterfly Photography in Rajaji
Rajaji National Park offers good opportunities for butterfly and nature photography.

Visitors should observe butterflies without disturbing them and follow all Forest Department, safari and wildlife regulations. Avoid handling butterflies, damaging vegetation or leaving the designated safari route.
Explore the Wildlife of Rajaji Tiger Reserve

Explore the Rich Flora of Rajaji Tiger Reserve

Rajaji National Park, now part of Rajaji Tiger Reserve, lies in the Shivalik Hills and Himalayan foothills of Uttarakhand. The reserve supports a diverse range of natural habitats, including Sal forests, mixed deciduous forests, riverine vegetation, scrublands, grasslands and subtropical pine forests.

During a Rajaji Jeep Safari, visitors can enjoy these varied landscapes and observe the rich plant life that supports the reserve's wildlife. From towering Sal trees and flowering Amaltas to riverine trees, shrubs and native grasses, the flora of Rajaji Tiger Reserve plays an important role in maintaining the ecological balance of this Himalayan foothill ecosystem.
Common Trees and Plants of Rajaji Tiger Reserve
Some commonly recorded or characteristic plant species found in Rajaji National Park and the surrounding reserve landscape include:

Sal (Shorea robusta), Rohini (Mallotus philippensis), Amaltas (Cassia fistula), Palash (Butea monosperma), Shisham (Dalbergia sissoo), Sandan (Ougeinia oojeinensis), Khair (Senegalia catechu), Arjun (Terminalia arjuna), Bamboo (Dendrocalamus strictus), Semul (Bombax ceiba), Chamaror (Ehretia laevis), Amla (Aonla) (Phyllanthus emblica), Ber (Ziziphus mauritiana), Chilla (Casearia tomentosa), Bel (Aegle marmelos) and Kachnar (Bauhinia variegata).
Experience the Natural Beauty of Rajaji

The diverse flora of Rajaji Tiger Reserve creates a beautiful setting for wildlife viewing, birdwatching, nature photography and jungle safari experiences. The forests, grasslands and riverine habitats provide food, shelter and breeding resources for numerous species of birds, mammals, insects and other wildlife.
A visit to Rajaji National Park offers an opportunity to appreciate not only its famous wildlife but also the fascinating plant communities that sustain this unique Himalayan foothill ecosystem.

Rajaji National Park, supports a rich diversity of wildlife across its Sal forests, deciduous forests, Khair-Sissoo woodlands, riverine habitats, grasslands, scrublands and pine forests. These varied habitats provide suitable conditions for a wide range of mammals and other wildlife.

Rajaji Tiger Reserve is home to several iconic mammal species, including the Asian Elephant, Bengal Tiger, Leopard, Chital, Sambar, Barking Deer, Goral, Nilgai and Wild Boar. Other mammals recorded in the Rajaji landscape include the Jungle Cat, Leopard Cat, Jackal, Striped Hyena, Sloth Bear, Himalayan Black Bear, Rhesus Macaque, Hanuman Langur, Yellow-throated Marten, Indian Hare, Pangolin and Indian Porcupine. The Rusty-spotted Cat has also been documented from the wider Rajaji landscape.
The reserve plays an important role in the conservation of Asian Elephants and Bengal Tigers under Project Elephant and Project Tiger. Rajaji was notified as a Tiger Reserve in 2015.

During a Rajaji Jeep Safari, visitors may have opportunities to observe these fascinating mammals in their natural habitats. Wildlife sightings depend on animal movements, habitat conditions, season and other natural factors and cannot be guaranteed.
Experience the Wildlife of Rajaji

The combination of Shivalik hills, river valleys, forests, grasslands and riverine habitats creates a diverse landscape for wildlife. During a Rajaji Jeep Safari, visitors may encounter elephants, deer, wild boar, langurs and other mammals, while sightings of tigers, leopards and other elusive species depend on natural animal movements.

A visit to Rajaji Tiger Reserve offers an opportunity to experience the rich biodiversity of the Himalayan foothills and appreciate the interconnected habitats that support its remarkable flora and fauna.

Rajaji Tiger Reserve in Uttarakhand supports a variety of reptiles associated with its forests, grasslands, rocky areas, streams and riverine habitats. These reptiles form an important part of the reserve's biodiversity and contribute to the ecological balance of the forest ecosystem.

Reptiles recorded or reported from the wider Rajaji landscape include the Indian Cobra, King Cobra, Indian Rock Python, Common Krait and Indian Monitor Lizard, along with other snakes, lizards and reptiles associated with different habitats.

During a Rajaji Jeep Safari, visitors may occasionally observe reptiles in suitable habitats. However, reptile and other wildlife sightings depend on season, weather, habitat conditions and natural animal movements and cannot be guaranteed.
